references.text: Job says that God reveals what is in darkness and brings the shadow of death into the light. This is an early expression of the same principle Jesus teaches: that what is hidden will be made manifest ([ref:Job 12:22|Job 12:22]).

The Preacher declares that God will bring every deed to judgment, including everything hidden, whether good or evil. This supports Jesus' words that nothing remains covered ([ref:Eccles 12:14|Ecclesiastes 12:14]).
Isaiah warns against those who try to hide their plans from the Lord and do their deeds in darkness. Yet God sees everything, and what is hidden will be revealed ([ref:Isa 29:15|Isaiah 29:15]).

Daniel praises God as the one who reveals deep and hidden things, knows what is in darkness, and with whom light dwells. This shows the divine principle that God uncovers all that is hidden ([ref:Dan 2:22|Daniel 2:22]).

Jesus' parallel statement in Matthew: "For there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known." Luke 12:2 is a close parallel to this verse ([ref:Matt 10:26|Matthew 10:26]).

In Mark, Jesus says: "For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not come to light." This confirms the same principle that all that is hidden will come into the light ([ref:Mark 4:22|Mark 4:22]).

An earlier statement by Jesus in Luke with the same message: "For there is nothing hidden that will not be made visible, and nothing concealed that will not be known and brought to light" ([ref:Luke 8:17|Luke 8:17]).
Paul writes about the day when God will judge the secrets of people through Jesus Christ. This emphasizes that what is covered will ultimately be revealed at judgment ([ref:Rom 2:16|Romans 2:16]).

Paul urges not to judge before the time, until the Lord comes and brings to light what is hidden in darkness and reveals the purposes of the heart. This reflects Jesus' words that what is hidden will be made known ([ref:1 Cor 4:5|1 Corinthians 4:5]).
